transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um... well, I guess I'm here because I've been having some issues with... elevators. 

I've just started planning my days around not using them, really. Like... I've been taking five flights of stairs at home instead. And I actually turned down a workshop I was supposed to do recently because it was in a high-rise. I even stopped going to see one of my older computer students, just because his building doesn't really have another option besides the elevator. So... yeah. I guess it's becoming a problem.
What is it about elevators that bothers you?

I guess just... getting stuck. I mean, I know a regular elevator in an office block is probably safe. But... when I look at the older doors in my apartment building, or at work... my mind just treats it like I'm about to get trapped in there. Or dropped. 

I know it sounds over the top, but... yeah. That's what happens.
Do you find yourself worrying about getting stuck or trapped in other situations, not just elevators?
No, not really. Just elevators.
Is it the enclosed space of the elevator itself that bothers you, or is it more the possibility of something going wrong with the elevator?
Um... I'm not really sure. I guess... maybe both? I just don't like them.
Have you ever felt anxious or uncomfortable in other small or enclosed spaces, like a car or a small room?
No. Cars are fine. Small rooms are fine. It's just the elevators.
Is there something specific that happens when you're in an elevator, like the doors closing or the movement, that triggers your fear?

Um... I don't know if it's the doors closing or the movement. It's just kind of... right away. Like, as soon as I walk toward one, or just hear the doors open. My chest gets tight, and my hands get sweaty. I just... I get this panic before I even have time to think about it.
Is your fear of elevators the same in all types of elevators, or is it worse in some compared to others?

Um... it varies, I guess. Like, I know a regular elevator in an office block is probably safe. But... the older ones, like the doors at my apartment building, or at work... I don't know. I just look at them and my mind kind of treats it like I'm about to get trapped in there. Or dropped. 

I mean, part of me knows that sounds kind of over the top. But... yeah. The old ones are worse.
Is it the idea of being in an elevator itself that scares you, or is it the possibility of something bad happening while you're in the elevator?
Um... I'm not really sure. I haven't really thought about it like that. I just... I just know I don't want to get in them.
Is it the elevator itself that you're afraid of, or the situation of being in a high-rise building?
Um... it's just the elevator. The building doesn't matter. I just... I don't like elevators.
Have you ever had a similar feeling of panic or anxiety in any other enclosed space that is not an elevator?
Um... no. Not really. Just... just the elevators.
Have you ever had a panic reaction to a similar mode of transportation, like an escalator?
No, escalators are fine. It's just elevators.
Do you think you would be afraid of being in a large, enclosed room that is not an elevator?
Um, no. I don't think so. Big rooms are fine.
Would you feel anxious or scared if you were in a situation where you were confined to a small space, but it wasn't an elevator?
Um, no... not really. I haven't noticed anything like that. It's really just the elevators.
Would you feel anxious if you were in a situation that simulated an elevator, like a small, enclosed space that moved vertically?
Um... I don't really know. I've never been in anything like that, so... I couldn't say. I just know I don't like regular elevators.
Would your fear of elevators change if you were in a building where you knew you could easily exit the elevator at any time if something went wrong
Um... I don't know. I guess maybe it would help a little? But... I haven't really thought about it. I just try to take the stairs anyway.
Would your fear of elevators be less if you were using one that only went up a few floors?
Um... I'm not sure. I mean, maybe a little? But... I still wouldn't want to get in one. I just... I don't really know.
Would you feel anxious if you were in a room that is the same size as an elevator, but does not move?
Um... probably not? I mean, if it's just a normal room that doesn't go anywhere... I guess I'd be fine. But... yeah, I haven't really paid attention to that.
Would you be afraid of using an elevator in a building where you are the only person using it?
Um... I couldn't really say. I've never... I haven't been in a situation like that before. So I don't know if it would make a difference.
Would your fear of elevators be less if you were using one that only went up a very short distance, like one or two floors?
Um... I don't think so. I mean, it's still an elevator, so... I just wouldn't want to get in it.
